# Casa — Home Assistant app

Canonical current-state documentation for AI agents working on this repository.
Code is the source of truth; these files are a map.

## Architecture

- [architecture/agent-taxonomy.md](architecture/agent-taxonomy.md): How an agent is declared, validated and looked up — tiers, required artifacts, and the registry.
- [architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md](architecture/background-job-direct-chat.md): A background job in the operator's direct chat — the start line and its Cancel, a specialist job's ask_operator questions and their buttons, a parked job's line, replies into a live job, the job-post ownership the engagement record keeps, and the retirement of a job's keyboards when it ends.
- [architecture/background-job-message-journal.md](architecture/background-job-message-journal.md): The operator-message journal of a background job — the per-job file an operator message is committed to before it is admitted, when an entry goes, the check of every entry against the session transcript at boot and at recovery, the one marked redelivery, and the lost-message notice of an ended job.
- [architecture/background-job-occupancy.md](architecture/background-job-occupancy.md): How many plugin-declared background jobs may be live or starting at once — one per installed plugin and one per plugin manifest name, whichever host kind runs it — and the claim that covers a start before its record exists.
- [architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md](architecture/background-job-quiet-runs.md): A plugin job declaring quietWhenScheduled — a run its schedule started opens no topic, posts no progress line, and is told nowhere when it completes unless it asked the operator something or was answered, while its plugin's delivered slots still reach the operator.
- [architecture/background-job-session.md](architecture/background-job-session.md): How a running background job's session works — the brief and every later write from one writer, the reader and the CLI's take-up echo, continuing, nudging and parking at a turn end, the one resume after a CLI death or a restart, auto-compaction and the job header, and the cost shown to the operator.
- [architecture/background-jobs.md](architecture/background-jobs.md): Plugin-declared background jobs — the casa.jobs declaration, the resident jobs block, start_job, specialist and resident-plugin worker launches, the progress tool, and the only reasons Casa ends a job.
- [architecture/callback-delivery.md](architecture/callback-delivery.md): The authorization-callback delivery half — the mtime-clocked publish-once spool, the per-flow attempt ledger and its ack protocol, the consumer verbs, and redelivery until receipt.
- [architecture/callbacks.md](architecture/callbacks.md): The public authorization-callback ingress — the unauthenticated GET route, declaration-bound consent, reconciliation, and the validated redirect base URL.
- [architecture/concurrency-model.md](architecture/concurrency-model.md): What runs concurrently — bus dequeue vs execution, session-key serialization, the lock inventory, and threaded vs loop work.
- [architecture/config-reconciliation.md](architecture/config-reconciliation.md): How the config tree is reconciled against image defaults — ownership rules, the per-entry merge, `${VAR}` placeholder semantics, and the declaration carried across a rewrite.
- [architecture/configuration.md](architecture/configuration.md): Where configuration comes from, what is version-controlled, what reload can pick up without a restart, and how secrets resolve.
- [architecture/configurator.md](architecture/configurator.md): The configurator as an image-owned delegate run in the operator's DM — its origins, the one lease and the busy refusal, the interrupted-run notice, the Restart now button, approval and erasure continuations, install time off the ceiling, the plugin-health hold and the step line.
- [architecture/delegate-answer-relay.md](architecture/delegate-answer-relay.md): A delegate's answer posted by Casa under the delegate's own header — the assistant chooses to relay it, Casa holds the delegate's words for it, posts them once, files the post for the delegate's desk, and what a failed send leaves.
- [architecture/delegation-announcements.md](architecture/delegation-announcements.md): What a finished delegation owes its creator — the delivery-acknowledged announcement, the answer retained for it, the boot replay's re-announcement, and how long the finished row is kept.
- [architecture/delegation.md](architecture/delegation.md): How one agent addresses and launches another — the delegation ACL and aliases, the depth cap, and the agent-spawn cap.
- [architecture/engagement-completion-gate.md](architecture/engagement-completion-gate.md): The completion gate — what a successful completion is refused over, why a message in flight is disclosed but never vetoed, and what the driver counts.
- [architecture/engagement-failure-and-restart.md](architecture/engagement-failure-and-restart.md): A launch that does not become a live engagement — which gate refused it, which arms answer the caller rather than the topic, what a graceful stop records against a launch, and what a restart does with a record.
- [architecture/engagement-finalization.md](architecture/engagement-finalization.md): How a durable engagement ends — the single-winner terminal transition, strict creation and terminal persistence, and the finalization side effects behind the flip.
- [architecture/engagement-inbound-disclosure.md](architecture/engagement-inbound-disclosure.md): What the operator is told about a message to a job that the job never read — one notice, from the seam when the job did not accept it or from the job's message journal once the job ended without reading it, in reply to the message in the direct chat or in the topic; no terminal outcome lists such messages.
- [architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md](architecture/engagement-launch-detach.md): How a background job's launch is separated from the tool call that launched it — the session opened and the brief queued before `pending`, the launch-death reporter for a launch that ends before its answer, what the engager is told, the stop's drains, and the one engagement-outcome envelope.
- [architecture/engagement-terminal-telling.md](architecture/engagement-terminal-telling.md): What a terminal engagement's topic and its engager are told — the outcome mark withheld until the topic was told, the unconfirmed-post disclosure, and the durable obligation to notify the party that asked.
- [architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md](architecture/engagement-transcript-reaping.md): Where a finished engagement's and a delegation's CLI transcripts are deleted — the retention, the run-confirmation gate the pass asks, what a terminal record names, what it never selects, and what it retries.
- [architecture/engagement-turn-admission.md](architecture/engagement-turn-admission.md): How a write is admitted into a live job's session — the registry decision taken immediately before the client call, the brief included, where the driver places it, and what it does not fence.
- [architecture/engagements.md](architecture/engagements.md): Durable engagements — their records, how one is launched, and the driver protocol.
- [architecture/eval-framework.md](architecture/eval-framework.md): The evaluation scaffolding — and the fact that its registry ships empty.
- [architecture/home-assistant-control.md](architecture/home-assistant-control.md): How an agent reads and changes the state of the house — and why the limits on that live in Home Assistant, not here.
- [architecture/hook-resolution.md](architecture/hook-resolution.md): How an agent's hooks are resolved in process, where the configurator's hooks come from, the read grant, and the path_scope tool-results rule.
- [architecture/http-surface.md](architecture/http-surface.md): The two HTTP servers, what each exposes, and how an inbound request is authenticated.
- [architecture/inbound-files.md](architecture/inbound-files.md): Files sent in the Telegram DM — the non-text handler, accepted kinds, the /data/agent-inbox folder, the default agent's read grant, list_inbound_files, retention.
- [architecture/job-triggers.md](architecture/job-triggers.md): A resident's scheduled trigger whose target is a plugin job — the entry's rails, the checks at write, load and registration, and a fire that starts the job through the one launcher with no resident turn.
- [architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md](architecture/jobs-and-delivery.md): Durable background jobs — execution vs delivery state, restart reconciliation, and what a graceful stop does to a live row.
- [architecture/mcp-and-tools.md](architecture/mcp-and-tools.md): How tools reach an agent through its in-process casa-framework server, where authorization for a tool call actually happens, and the optional n8n MCP server.
- [architecture/memory-capture.md](architecture/memory-capture.md): Capture — how each turn's words are made durable in the memory store as they happen, with the spool fallback, and which text is eligible at all — write-trust, a delegated answer's completeness, and the specialists whose output is kept out.
- [architecture/memory-export-restore.md](architecture/memory-export-restore.md): The memory export — a verified copy of the store's rows from the terminal, every night and before a schema migration — and the restore that replaces all of memory with one, validated and staged at the request and built, wiped and installed by the container-start step.
- [architecture/memory-labelling.md](architecture/memory-labelling.md): Item labelling — how each captured item is labelled, with its occurrence key, its tier classification, and the notes and time envelope that never reach it.
- [architecture/memory-lifecycle.md](architecture/memory-lifecycle.md): Session lifecycle — the freshness windows, how an explicit reset retires a session under its retirement claim, and how long an SDK transcript is kept (run confirmation and retention).
- [architecture/memory-scoping.md](architecture/memory-scoping.md): Which stored facts a given reader gets back — read clearance per channel and sender, one ledger per served clearance written only from what it can read, the per-object check on every read path, and who may steer a job at the clearance it inherited.
- [architecture/memory-serving.md](architecture/memory-serving.md): Serving memory — the view of a ledger a session is served at its start (whole, or its index past the budget), frozen for the session, and the correction note on every turn of every memory role.
- [architecture/memory-store.md](architecture/memory-store.md): The SQLite memory store and its one connection owner, the boot check that leaves memory unavailable rather than empty, and the registry of every place memory lives with its export, restore and wipe rules.
- [architecture/memory-tools.md](architecture/memory-tools.md): The memory tools — search the saved conversation (and the derived search index behind it), browse a day, open ledger entries by id, mark a correction — and the engager query's read, each filtered per object at the reader's clearance.
- [architecture/memory-wipe.md](architecture/memory-wipe.md): The operator-consented memory wipe — its three doors and the consent each demands, the intent and the app restart, the container-start step that erases exactly the registry, notification-only boot after a failed attempt, the courtesy line in the window before the restart, and why a job open at the wipe ends rather than resumes.
- [architecture/memory-writer.md](architecture/memory-writer.md): The memory writer — the one background worker that files captured events into the ledgers, the one pending predicate, the commit and its three checks, correction marks that re-open, crash recovery, classification, failures, the nightly pass and the size meter.
- [architecture/memory.md](architecture/memory.md): A one-hop map of Casa's built-in long-term memory — capture, the store, the writer and its ledgers, scoping, serving, the tools, and the whole-memory operations — and which document owns each.
- [architecture/observability.md](architecture/observability.md): How work is traced across components, what reaches a log, and what the health surfaces actually assert.
- [architecture/output-boundary.md](architecture/output-boundary.md): One place for per-turn output policy — the turn scope, admission of model text at the Telegram transport, the read-before-describe disclosure, and the note a stored payload carries to the turn that sends it.
- [architecture/output-scope-properties.md](architecture/output-scope-properties.md): What a turn's scope decides about the turn itself — whether it streams, whether its final reply is closing silence (the
- [architecture/overview.md](architecture/overview.md): What Casa is made of — supervised services, the three agent tiers, and where configuration enters.
- [architecture/persistent-state.md](architecture/persistent-state.md): What the application writes to disk, how it treats a missing or corrupt file, and what that means for recovery.
- [architecture/persona-lifecycle.md](architecture/persona-lifecycle.md): How a persona arrives, is approved, and leaves — consent-bound install, the approved roots, removal by reference scan, and the operator-run sweep.
- [architecture/personality.md](architecture/personality.md): What an agent is versus how it presents — role artifacts, personas, bindings, and which prompt is actually served.
- [architecture/plugin-access-profiles.md](architecture/plugin-access-profiles.md): How an assignment gives an agent a subset of a plugin's tools — the registry profiles map, casa.profiles and casa.requires, the plan every options build enforces through a PreToolUse barrier, and what the configurator is told about recommendations.
- [architecture/plugin-authorization.md](architecture/plugin-authorization.md): What a protected plugin tool call needs before it runs — the single-use grant it consumes, the challenge that mints it, who may answer, and what retires an unanswered one.
- [architecture/plugin-continuations.md](architecture/plugin-continuations.md): How a plugin's work that outlives one turn is carried on in fresh turns of its specialist — the continuation queue, the origin rebuilt from a binding, the relay of the answer up the requester chain, a role's desk-context switch, and the once-a-minute driver sweep.
- [architecture/plugin-delivered-files.md](architecture/plugin-delivered-files.md): A file a plugin's capability tool delivers — the operator_file slot, its deposit, the claim from the plugin outbox under the kind's media policy, and the delivered name a deposit may carry.
- [architecture/plugin-delivered-slots.md](architecture/plugin-delivered-slots.md): A slot a plugin's capability tool delivers — a link, a message or a file Casa posts to the operator's chat, labelled, the result replaced by a receipt — and the body-free echo the resident's conversation sees.
- [architecture/plugin-delivery-repeats.md](architecture/plugin-delivery-repeats.md): A delivered slot's deposit that carries a key — a repeated delivery of a key Casa already delivered sends nothing and returns the original receipt, so a plugin job cut between posting and recording does not post twice.
- [architecture/plugin-erase-episode.md](architecture/plugin-erase-episode.md): How Casa runs a plugin's chosen eraser once an erase_data=true call consumed the operator's Erase choice — the Casa-dispatched erase turn and its plugin_erase marker, the broker hooks that bind it to its own run, the fence on the erasing plugin's other tools, the wait bound, and the erasure record per plugin.
- [architecture/plugin-erasure.md](architecture/plugin-erasure.md): How an uninstall erases a plugin's data first — the casa.eraseTool and casa.eraseDataOnlyTool fields and their result convention, Casa's question offering the declared erase kinds, the finishing call that removes only after a complete erasure, and the plugin-env.conf references cleared after Erase everything.
- [architecture/plugin-events.md](architecture/plugin-events.md): Plugin-emitted domain events — casa-minted generations, per-subscriber delivery receipts, and consent-gated headless wakes.
- [architecture/plugin-handoff.md](architecture/plugin-handoff.md): The folder files move through between plugins — /data/handoff, publish and capture (the vendored casa_handoff contract), the sweep, share_inbound_file's handoff side.
- [architecture/plugin-health.md](architecture/plugin-health.md): How a plugin's problems reach the operator — the standing health report, the notice and DM with their dedup marks, and the status tool.
- [architecture/plugin-mutation-tools.md](architecture/plugin-mutation-tools.md): What the plugin and specialist mutation tools guarantee — the commit-then-converge ordering and what an envelope may claim about an integration.
- [architecture/plugin-operator-calls.md](architecture/plugin-operator-calls.md): What a plugin's own code asks Casa during one of its declared callsCasa calls — whom the call serves (its binding), run admission from the operator's own words and its confirmation, a continuation for a run, a delivered slot's outcome, and the check of one browsing action.
- [architecture/plugin-removal.md](architecture/plugin-removal.md): What a committed plugin removal discloses about what it leaves behind — that the plugin's CLI-managed persistent data may remain and no provider revocation was performed, whether plugin_remove, a specialist bundle's owned-set swap or a bundle compensation reports it.
- [architecture/plugin-result-contract.md](architecture/plugin-result-contract.md): The plugin result contract and the escrow broker — non-adopters refused before they run, a declared capability deposited with Casa and redeemed by reference.
- [architecture/plugin-runtime.md](architecture/plugin-runtime.md): The environment a plugin's MCP servers need before an agent can use it, plus the env-conf and media side channels.
- [architecture/plugin-secret-exploration.md](architecture/plugin-secret-exploration.md): How a plugin's required secrets are found — the vault exploration a mutation result carries, the configurator's two vault tools, their shared projection of field ids, roles and types (never an operator-typed string), and the classified op failure.
- [architecture/plugin-setup-dispatch-gate.md](architecture/plugin-setup-dispatch-gate.md): The gate a released setup obligation passes through before dispatch — the recomputation of the applied state a reconcile has written, and the overlay reads that fence the bus send.
- [architecture/plugin-setup-turn.md](architecture/plugin-setup-turn.md): The dispatched setup turn — what it evidences, how a courier turn's delegation is correlated, and the operator identity it carries for the role it is addressed to.
- [architecture/plugin-setup.md](architecture/plugin-setup.md): Who runs a plugin's declared setup tool — the single-runner obligation and the consent verdict that releases it.
- [architecture/plugin-stop.md](architecture/plugin-stop.md): The Stop — a specialist's own work (a browsing request) stopped at once with no model turn and no desk — the casa.stopTool declaration and Casa's direct call of it, the Stop on a request's card, a proposal button that stores the stop tool, the resident's stop_work tool, one flight per request, the card mark and the one line, and the continuations a stop drops.
- [architecture/plugin-triggers.md](architecture/plugin-triggers.md): What a plugin's declared webhook must satisfy before it routes — the overlay, its preconditions, and the operator approval gating them.
- [architecture/plugins.md](architecture/plugins.md): How a plugin becomes usable — registry, content-addressed store, artifact identity, and which tools are protected.
- [architecture/prompt-file-guards.md](architecture/prompt-file-guards.md): The per-agent prompt files a compiled bundle makes dead — response_shape.yaml and prompts/system.md — and the file-tool guards that refuse an edit to them.
- [architecture/reminders.md](architecture/reminders.md): How an agent comes to nudge someone later — entry ownership, the narrow writer, delivery, and the sweep that redeems a past-dated one-shot the process was down for.
- [architecture/scheduled-asks.md](architecture/scheduled-asks.md): A scheduled question as a durable obligation — its record on disk, its terminal delivery back to the session that asked, and its manners in the operator's attention lane.
- [architecture/scheduled-prompt-endings.md](architecture/scheduled-prompt-endings.md): The convention that closes a scheduled prompt — which prompts ask the turn for silence, and how the tools the turn calls decide the question.
- [architecture/scratchpad.md](architecture/scratchpad.md): The scratchpad tool of a delegated client and of a background job's session — whose pad it reaches, when a pad goes, a job pad's file, its plain line operations and the bound on its replies.
- [architecture/sdk-client-pool.md](architecture/sdk-client-pool.md): The life of the warm, conversation-bound client a turn runs on.
- [architecture/specialist-bundle-recovery.md](architecture/specialist-bundle-recovery.md): What a specialist bundle transaction does when it does not succeed — the pre-journal refusals, the sync-phase and sequencer compensations, the boot replay and quarantine pass, the age sweeps that follow it, and the race and failed-rotation refusals.
- [architecture/specialist-bundle-transactions.md](architecture/specialist-bundle-transactions.md): What happens to an installed specialist after its install — the upgrade, rollback and uninstall transactions, the owned-plugin generation each publishes, and the crash journal that makes a bundle transaction recoverable.
- [architecture/specialist-desk-reply.md](architecture/specialist-desk-reply.md): A specialist desk turn's reply — the labelled, admitted reply of the specialist's own words, the closing-silence and sentinel rules, the one notice a turn with no proven outcome ends in, the one emitter every line goes through, the resident's body-free echo, and the approval continuation that returns to the desk.
- [architecture/specialist-desk.md](architecture/specialist-desk.md): The specialist desk — the operator's swipe-reply on a specialist's post reaches that specialist as one desk turn (never the resident), the post map every delivered message is filed in, the bounded dialogue log a desk keeps and its one-use-at-a-time lock, and the note a reply the desk does not take carries.
- [architecture/specialist-handoff.md](architecture/specialist-handoff.md): A specialist answering a request hands part of it to another specialist and gets the answer back — the hand_off tool, the requester chain and the operator's words every delegated run carries, the mechanical bounds, the permit, and the requester's ceiling a hand-off pauses.
- [architecture/specialist-instance-tuples.md](architecture/specialist-instance-tuples.md): The instance tuples a specialist install leaves behind — what a tuple snapshot may hold and the digest derived from it, a pending candidate and the inputs its re-commit takes, and what boot does with a damaged tuple.
- [architecture/specialist-job-start.md](architecture/specialist-job-start.md): A specialist starts a background job its own plugins declare, hosted on itself, from a desk or delegated turn — the build that offers start_job, the call-time host resolution, the two launch gates a self-start skips, and the turn's origin the job runs with.
- [architecture/specialist-lifecycle.md](architecture/specialist-lifecycle.md): Specialist install — the content-addressed store, install identity, consent receipts and materialization.
- [architecture/specialist-open-conversations.md](architecture/specialist-open-conversations.md): What each change to an installed specialist does to its open conversations — the warning a persona apply, upgrade, rollback or uninstall returns first, the acknowledgement carried in the call, and the close after an uninstall commits.
- [architecture/stored-call-buttons.md](architecture/stored-call-buttons.md): Stored-call buttons — a specialist's plugin proposes a decision as buttons (the operator_proposal delivered kind), a tap is admitted by a fail-closed chain and re-checked under the desk lock on one captured build input, one pinned specialist turn executes exactly the stored call, the plugin's response is the labelled receipt, and the resident learns of it by one body-free line.
- [architecture/stored-call-next-card.md](architecture/stored-call-next-card.md): Stored-call buttons, what a tap shows besides its receipt — the next card a safe stored call returns beside its receipt (#1302), judged and registered as a deposit, the same card shown in place of the tapped one by an edit of the tapped message (#1339), falling back to the receipt and a new card, a file button that keeps its card (#1362), a Close button whose tap only removes the card's buttons (#1375), and the plain pages a card may bring before it (#1377).
- [architecture/stored-call-termination.md](architecture/stored-call-termination.md): Stored-call buttons, the pinned turn's end — the PinnedRun controller owns the run's processes and kills and confirms them under a bound, every end goes through one shielded release path, and an unconfirmed termination faults the desk until a restart.
- [architecture/telegram-failures.md](architecture/telegram-failures.md): The Telegram channel's failure behavior — wrong or missing webhook secrets, duplicate updates, unavailable transports and the other wrong-input paths; split out of telegram.md at the corpus ceiling (#1206).
- [architecture/telegram-rendering.md](architecture/telegram-rendering.md): How an answer is rendered for Telegram — the markdown grammar and tables, pagination to the platform's budgets, link-destination fallbacks, and the shared UTF-16 measurement.
- [architecture/telegram.md](architecture/telegram.md): How Telegram messages become turns — transports, authentication, and keyboards.
- [architecture/tool-questions.md](architecture/tool-questions.md): The question lifecycle — what ask_user's operator-DM arm and wipe_memory's consent keyboard report when the question cannot be delivered or is over before the tool returns; split out of tools-interface.md at the corpus ceiling (#1153).
- [architecture/tools-interface.md](architecture/tools-interface.md): The mutation interface — the one tool registry, result envelopes, and which failures roll back versus report.
- [architecture/trigger-secrets.md](architecture/trigger-secrets.md): The secrets that authenticate webhook triggers — who mints one and when, the mint receipt and provenance, the per-slot reload report, and what is not retired.
- [architecture/triggers.md](architecture/triggers.md): What makes an agent act without a person speaking — a resident's scheduled and webhook triggers, and who may write the file they live in.
- [architecture/turn-limits.md](architecture/turn-limits.md): What bounds a resident turn — the stop at its turn limit, the one line Casa adds about it and where that line goes, and the limits the residents run with.
- [architecture/turn-loop.md](architecture/turn-loop.md): How one inbound message becomes one agent turn — what it assembles and how its model call is retried.
- [architecture/vault-drop-off.md](architecture/vault-drop-off.md): How a sign-in link reaches the plugin tool that consumes it without a delegation brief — the casa.dropOffs field, the Casa-titled and tagged vault item, and the assistant's vault_drop_off tool that writes only that item and never returns or logs the value.
- [architecture/voice-delivery.md](architecture/voice-delivery.md): The leased claim/acknowledge protocol that gets a deferred voice answer to a device — attempts, leases, per-device ordering, the fixed bounds, and result disclosure.
- [architecture/voice.md](architecture/voice.md): How speech becomes a turn and the answer gets back — transports, auth, turn budget, deferred delivery.
- [architecture/webhook-delivery.md](architecture/webhook-delivery.md): Where a plugin webhook fire's reply goes — the deliver opt-in, the tools such a turn is offered, and the operator_always value under which no fire ends silent.

## Reference

- [reference/casa-browser-actions.md](reference/casa-browser-actions.md): The Casa Browser action gate — which agent actions are checked, the packet the check sees, verdicts bound to the packet's digest and applied once, the floor F1–F9 with the pacer's guard and the dispatch journal, and sign-in codes.
- [reference/casa-browser-approvals.md](reference/casa-browser-approvals.md): The Casa Browser app's questions to the operator — the question an ask verdict freezes, its view and confirm rules, the operator's answer applied once, the tap-time re-judgement and final read, the live view from a question, login questions and a question's hour.
- [reference/casa-browser-browser.md](reference/casa-browser-browser.md): The Casa Browser app's Chrome runtime — the browser-user launcher behind the controller's Patchright, the launch contract, sessions and profiles, the managed Chrome policy, the virtual display and human pacing.
- [reference/casa-browser-contract.md](reference/casa-browser-contract.md): The Casa Browser protocol v1 contract as a trusted caller (Casa's browsing plugin) relies on it — every request and reply member, bound, error code, event kind and the locale contract, gathered in one place, with the fake controller that serves the same wire.
- [reference/casa-browser-credentials.md](reference/casa-browser-credentials.md): The Casa Browser credential broker, vault facade, login RPC flow, the guest's role (a warning), journal recovery and notice imports.
- [reference/casa-browser-files.md](reference/casa-browser-files.md): The Casa Browser app's downloads and files — link fetches decided hop by hop through the enforcing proxy, browser downloads, safe file names and types, bounds, archives, and delivery records.
- [reference/casa-browser-ingress.md](reference/casa-browser-ingress.md): The Casa Browser ingress UI and W+ live view — nginx admitting only HA's ingress peer, nonce-checked forms, pairing, sites and setup pages, grants and claims, the one viewer, the screen lock, window fit and verified restore, tap-to-type input, reconnect, and the Done screen.
- [reference/casa-browser-live-states.md](reference/casa-browser-live-states.md): The Casa Browser run controller around a live view — the states a run moves through, the claim, what any end of a view releases, and what Done does.
- [reference/casa-browser-observations.md](reference/casa-browser-observations.md): What a model and the operator may see of a page in the Casa Browser app — observations behind the page-view gate, masked text, opaque handles, how an element is named, and screenshots under one capture rule.
- [reference/casa-browser-runs.md](reference/casa-browser-runs.md): The Casa Browser run controller — one leased run at a time, its sessions, policy installs bound to the proxy start, the broker and driver sequences, live-view states, and teardown confirmed before a run ends.
- [reference/casa-browser-runtime.md](reference/casa-browser-runtime.md): The Casa Browser app's runtime enforcement — the kernel egress floor per service user, public-destination checks, and the enforcing TLS proxy with its pinned resolution, withdrawal of authority, login-lease closure, broker listener and control plane.
- [reference/casa-browser-signin.md](reference/casa-browser-signin.md): Signing in to a site that is not set up from one operator tap (the sign-in card, its Yes registering exactly the card's origin), signing in on a page of a registered site that is not its start page (the look, its sign_in check and its binding), and saving a login typed in the live view, an email-only one included.
- [reference/casa-browser.md](reference/casa-browser.md): The Casa Browser app — its options and root bootstrap, durable state and retention, the /v1 protocol with pairing and the admission digest, and the address check and request policy.
- [reference/operator-options.md](reference/operator-options.md): The option-by-option operator contract — key, env var, consumer, default, restart-vs-reload.

## Doctrine

- [doctrine/operating-casa.md](doctrine/operating-casa.md): How an agent running inside Casa should behave, and which property of the system each rule follows from.
- [doctrine/publishing.md](doctrine/publishing.md): The one rule that decides whether a fact may be written down in this repository.
- [doctrine/working-on-casa.md](doctrine/working-on-casa.md): How to change this repository without breaking it, and how to establish that a claim about it is true.

- [contributing/doc-contract.md](contributing/doc-contract.md): The shape a document takes, and which of its rules CI enforces versus a reviewer.
